<!-- pr-reviewer: 846c9a08c63a4b708227ce846d84d6f1d17baa3f -->
**Needs changes before merge** - `floor_at` can report a floor over a column a cut has already removed (invented material).

**What looks good**
- Shell floor is the lowest crossing of the parity column (`field_floor.rs:38-40`): right for multiple shells and undercuts; NaN/inf columns are `Unreadable`, a column beside the stock is `NoMaterial`, an `Open` column is `Unreadable`. No unwrap/panic; `saturating_add` on the cell index.
- The `FloorRead` enum is `#[must_use]`-friendly and the refusal is named. Provenance line present, new file is 59 lines, nothing wired in yet.
- The #646 "bit for bit" wording is softened as promised.

**Local results (PR merged with current upstream/main; the merge only touched AGENTS.md, no conflicts)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (whole crate): 351 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. This includes field_floor 2/2, field_carry 3/3, stock_backend_parity, stock_columns.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run: app suites (PR only touches sim, nothing wired).

**Requested before merge**
1. `field_floor.rs:44-50`: the cut test reads the claim of the cell that holds `(x, y)`, but a claim is `> 0` only when the cell CENTER is inside the tool. A query point inside the cut but within half a cell of the cut wall, on the side where the cell center is outside the tool, gets `Floor(z)` for a column that is air. I reproduced it with your own fixture (cell 0.5, slot through the plate with tool radius 2.2, so the slot spans y 3.8 to 8.2, query x = 10.25):
```
y=3.81 (in slot)  -> Floor(-6.0)      should be refused
y=3.90 (in slot)  -> Floor(-6.0)      should be refused
y=3.99 (in slot)  -> Floor(-6.0)      should be refused
y=4.01 (in slot)  -> CutFromBelow
y=8.10 (in slot)  -> Floor(-6.0)      should be refused
y=8.19 (in slot)  -> Floor(-5.999999999999999)
```
   That is exactly the "wrong floor invents air / acquits a gouge" failure. Fix: look at the 3x3 (or at least the 2x2 nearest) neighbouring XY cells as well as the z neighbours, so any claimed cell within a cell of the point refuses; or test the swept distance at the actual `(x, y, z)`. Add a pin for a point inside the wall band (the existing test uses 10.25, 6.25, mid-slot, and wall-aligned cells, so it cannot see this).
2. Same line, sub-cell thickness: for a cut that removes only a thin layer of the floor (thinner than a cell, with no cell centre inside it) the check also misses, giving a floor lower than the real one. The 3-cell z window helps only when a centre falls inside the cut. If the rule stays cell-based, state in the module doc that it is conservative only for cuts at least a cell thick, or use the point-exact test from item 1 and the problem goes away.
3. Docs (`field_floor.rs:1-15`): "exact" / "bit-exact" is stronger than what the code returns (the mid-wall probe above returned -5.999999999999999). Say "to rounding", as you did for #646.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- Nothing calls `floor_at` yet, so there is no silent-ignore path today; when step C wires it, every caller must match all four `FloorRead` arms (no `_ =>`).
- Body is complete: `Changelog: none`, `Refs #637`, conventional subjects. PR is stacked on #646, merge that first.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: c5cce5641a1bd8f1f48f53f39317799b231635fc -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The blocker from the review at 846c9a08 is fixed.

**The fix, checked**
- Sign and units: `claim_record`/`claim` (field_batch.rs) store `min(-phi, cap)` where `phi` is the signed tool distance (negative inside the tool). So `cut_at(key) > -cell` means the tool came within one cell of that centre. `claim` stores every cell with `phi < cap`, and `validate_shell` rejects `band == 0` (field.rs:334), so `cap >= cell` and every cell with `phi < cell` has a stored claim. Unclaimed cells read `-inf`, which never trips the test.
- Sufficiency: a point inside the swept volume lies at most (sqrt(3)/2)·cell from the centre of its own cell, and the distance field is 1-Lipschitz, so that centre has `phi <= 0.866·cell`, i.e. claim `>= -0.866·cell > -cell`. The slack (0.134·cell) also covers the golden-section residual, which is far below a cell. The own cell is the middle of the 3x3x3 block, so the neighbours are extra margin.
- Block position: `iz = cell_of(z, ...)` uses the floor z from the shell crossing, with `ix, iy` from the query. That is the right point. A shell crossing lies inside the shell box, which `region_of` covers (dilated by cap+3+2 cells), so there is no clipped-window loss; there is no per-field border clipping in `floor_at`, `cut_at` just reads a missing brick as `-inf`. `saturating_add` on the indices is fine.
- Pinning test `a_point_inside_a_cut_near_its_wall_is_refused_too` covers y 3.81/3.9/3.99/4.01/6.0/8.1/8.19, and y 0.75 stays exactly `Floor(-6.0)`.

**Local results (merged with fresh upstream/main, clean merge, no conflicts)**
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (whole crate): all suites pass, no failures. Unit 65; field_floor 3; field_carry 3; stock_carry 7; stock_sdf_cut 12; stock_sdf 9; stock_backend_parity 13; all remaining integration suites ok; 1 ignored in fixture_mesh, 1 in fixture_mesh_posed, 1 in hidden_rest_banded (pre-existing ignores).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No build.rs, `.github`, scripts or dependency changes in the diff.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The refusal is conservative: any tool pass within one cell of the floor point refuses the column, including a cut that stops a fraction of a cell above the floor, or a wall-hugging pass that never reaches it. That is the safe direction and matches the docs ("refused by name"). A shallow slot a full cell or more above the floor does not trigger it. A caller that clamps columns beside a finish pass will see `CutFromBelow` on those columns; the `cut_downs` companion (#637 option 1) is the planned way to lift it.
- The `Floor(z)` doc says "exact to rounding", which now holds for every returned value.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
